instruction.name: xvdiv.hu
instruction.description: Divide each unsigned 16-bit element in `a` by the corresponding element in `b`.

experiments.name: operand dependency chain
experiments.init: li.d $r4, 1; xvreplgr2vr.b $xr0, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; xvreplgr2vr.b $xr1, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; xvreplgr2vr.b $xr2, $r4

latencies.notes: Data-dependent, and a ladder rather than a set of discrete classes: latency = 5 + (64/16)*(6 + floor(bits(|quotient|)/4)), that is 5 + 4*(6 + n) with n the number of complete four-bit quotient digits. The minimum is 17 with a zero dividend and the maximum is 45 at a 16-bit quotient. LSX and LASX are identical for every element width although LASX carries twice the lanes, so the lanes and both 128-bit halves are refined in parallel and only the element width sets the per-bit rate, 16 quotient bits per cycle in aggregate. The unit divides magnitudes, skips trailing zero digits (2^40 / 1 still costs 11) and only pays for active lanes (one active lane in vdiv.bu measures 34 against 69 with every lane active). Measured with the drift-free chain `xvdiv.hu $xr0, $xr0, $xr1` and divisor 1, which returns the dividend unchanged. The cases array holds named sample points on this ladder, not an exhaustive classification.

experiment.name: no active lane or zero dividend
experiment.init: li.d $r4, 0; xvreplgr2vr.h $xr0, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; xvreplgr2vr.h $xr1, $r4; li.d $r4, 0; xvreplgr2vr.d $xr2, $r4; li.d $r4, 0; xvreplgr2vr.h $xr3, $r4
experiment.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 800 --unroll2 1600 --iters 40 --warmup 10 --reps 3 --init 'li.d $r4, 0; xvreplgr2vr.h $xr0, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; xvreplgr2vr.h $xr1, $r4; li.d $r4, 0; xvreplgr2vr.d $xr2, $r4; li.d $r4, 0; xvreplgr2vr.h $xr3, $r4' --asm 'xvdiv.hu $xr0, $xr0, $xr1'

throughput.notes: Range over the same pairs: min CPI 7.50 at 0/1, max CPI 21.50 at 65535/1. Sample uses 1/1.

notes: LASX variable-latency integer divide/modulo. Latency uses an element-0 reset helper; throughput uses 8 independent lanes. Ranges cover positive operands including powers of two and max values. Both vector sources are recorded separately; they share the same result path where the hardware is symmetric.
